Subject: Private offer request — dynamic rebate clauses + channel pass-through

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week. We've run this across our infra team and procurement and are ready to get a private offer in place, but we have a couple of asks before procurement can issue a PO:

- We need a dynamic rebate clause that triggers a retroactive credit when 12-month usage ramps exceed the commit by >20% (customer-side accelerator).
- We also require a clear channel pass-through calculation for our authorized reseller, CloudWave Resellers — procurement must see netback at the reseller level (their margin expectations are baked into our SOW).

Attached is the SOW and an initial procurement checklist (Nebula_SOW.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood supports: (a) conditional retro credits, (b) explicit line in the PO for partner netback rate, and (c) a mechanism for retrospective true-ups?

Our timeline: target signature by EOD 2027-03-05. If we can get terms this week, procurement will circulate a populated PO.

Best,
Elena Mendez
Senior Procurement Manager
Nebula AI

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mendez <elena.m@nebulaai.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer request — dynamic rebate clauses + channel pass-through

Hi Elena — thanks for the SOW and the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes (we can do a conditional retro credit), yes (we can publish a partner netback line in the PO), and yes (we support retrospective true-ups with either monthly or quarterly cadence).

A few clarifying points so we align on mechanics:

1) Accelerator (retro) trigger: we typically do a 12-month lookback and credit the difference between committed spend and billed usage above the 120% threshold. Credit is applied at list-price token units unless the customer requests partner-adjusted netback (see 3).

2) Credit cadence options: monthly (pro-rated) or quarterly (single reconciliation). Monthly is cleaner for accounting; quarterly reduces churn on settlements.

3) Channel netting: we can add a "Partner Pass-Through Rate" line in the PO; that rate will be multiplied against list price to compute the reseller netback. We need the partner margin percentage from you to bake into the term (e.g., 12% pass-through leaves 88% to Redwood pre-tax).

4) Compliance and audit: if you need supporting invoices for the reseller, we can produce an auditor CSV with token-by-token billing and pass-through calculations.

I've attached a short term sheet for a private offer to illustrate the language (Redwood_PO_Termsheet_v1.pdf). Can you confirm the reseller's pass-through % and whether you prefer monthly or quarterly true-ups?

If it's easier, I'm happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync with procurement + CloudWave to finalize.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi Vivek — thanks for the quick reply and the term sheet. Procurement reviewed and has two redline asks:

- They want the pass-through rate locked at 12% (CloudWave requires a floor of 10% but Nebula commits to 12% to secure preferred reseller status).
- For accelerator credits, procurement requests quarterly reconciliation with a 30-day payout window from the reconciliation date.

Also, CloudWave forwarded their margin schedule; procurement asked that Redwood include a short appendix in the PO showing the netback math for a sample month (we attached their template via the partners alias).

We intend to route the populated PO via DocuSign. Here's the draft DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/nebulaai/po/ABC-8237

Can you confirm acceptance of the two redlines and the appendix requirement? If accepted, we'll push the DocuSign envelope today.

Thanks,
Nebula Procurement

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -07:00

Sergio / Irene — looping you both in. Nebula is asking for: 12% pass-through floor, quarterly reconciliation with a 30-day payout, and an appendix that demonstrates the reseller netback calculation for a sample month.

Quick thoughts:
- Option A (standard): Accept 12% pass-through, quarterly true-up, Redwood issues credit at list price and the appendix shows list-price math. Minimal legal churn, no change to our billing flows.
- Option B (partner-adjusted): Accept 12% pass-through but compute accelerator credits using netback-adjusted pricing (i.e., apply partner pass-through first, then credit). This protects partner economics but lowers Redwood exposure.

We need finance to run a 12-month scenario for both options and confirm impact on unit economics. Irene, can you run a quick waterfall showing realized revenue under both A and B (include tax treatment and timing of credits)? Sergio, if ops needs changes to invoice delivery or the audit CSV, call that out.

If we accept, I suggest we push the term sheet updated with Appendix A and commit to quarterly reconciliations. Procurement wants DocuSign today.

Thanks,
Vivek
